issues.description: Method Stock.add(String): The UML in problem_statement.md declares Stock.add(String) with return type void, while both the template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) and the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) define public int add(String). This mismatch between the problem specification and the provided code can confuse students about the expected return value and behaviour of Stock.add (e.g., whether it should return the new quantity or be void), and may lead to incorrect implementations or failed compilations if students follow the UML instead of the code/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and code consistent. Prefer updating the UML in problem_statement.md to declare +add(String): int to match the template and solution (and tests). Alternatively, if the intended behaviour is void, change the template and solution method signatures to public void add(String) and update all callers/tests accordingly. Recommended action: change problem_statement.md UML to +add(String): int and document that the method returns the updated quantity (or -1 if not found).
